tagline: North with the Pend Oreille into the Forgotten Corner.
intro: The Pend Oreille flows north toward Canada, and from Tiger SR 31 goes along with it, beside the river and the railroad through Ione and Metaline. It crosses into Metaline Falls under Washington Rock, where the Selkirk peaks rise more than 1,000 feet above the water within a mile of town, and winds on past Crescent Lake and Boundary Lake to the border, the easternmost crossing in Washington.
Lead ore gave Metaline its name. Mining began in 1886, and the district grew into the state's largest producer of lead and zinc. The International Selkirk Loop calls this the Forgotten Corner.
season: The International Selkirk Loop says any season is the best time to visit.

moments.title: Tiger
moments.text: George Tiger started a river landing here in 1899, and the old store and post office, now a seasonal museum, is the only building left of the town.

moments.title: Metaline Falls
moments.text: When the FBI arrested George Kubota, the town's Japanese-American hardware man, in 1942, the newspaper and most of the town vouched for him, and he was let go.

moments.title: Gardner Cave
moments.text: Ed Gardner said the ground gave way under him and his horse here in 1899, and he kept his moonshine in the cave, which held a steady 39 degrees.

practical: Tours of Gardner Cave at Crawford State Park need a reservation.
